title: Seed database is a cache performance scenario
description: The ordered workload proves the authored semantic outcome and performance declaration.

injection.target: seeded client connect and sync dispatch

parameters.scenario: start from a portable seed and perform authenticated connect, delta, and rebuild
parameters.defect: authorize or synchronize from seed metadata through a separate seed-only mode

injection.target: portable seed scope and row export

parameters.scenario: add an auth-scoped row and an undeclared scope to an otherwise valid export
parameters.defect: infer portability from row presence instead of server-declared portable scope authority

parameters.scenario: install a seed row set with matching rows but no verified boundary, generation, cardinality, or digest metadata
parameters.defect: treat the rows as incrementally resumable without continuation receipt verification

injection.target: portable seed export transaction and connection

parameters.scenario: commit a source change while an export reads manifest, scope, rows, digest, boundary, retention, and receipt
parameters.defect: mix physical connections or transactions or read live post-snapshot state outside SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE

injection.target: seed page token and receipt conversion verifier

parameters.scenario: reuse a page token across exports, transactions, scopes, generations, boundaries, ordinals, or limits and pass a receipt directly as cursor
parameters.defect: accept cross-context continuation or bypass authenticated connect and current assignment validation

parameters.scenario: remove a row, alter a digest, skip a page or receipt, corrupt SQLite, add queue data, or change final hash
parameters.defect: publish the artifact despite a failed or skipped required verification

assertions.description: The ordered workload produces the complete authored durable semantic outcome without partial state.
Every declared budget or measurement records all configured strata and required metrics.
The portable-seed authority control detects an exported row or scope that the server did not declare portable.
The staged portable seed resumes only with verified continuation metadata.
The portable seed retains one snapshot-consistent export boundary.
Portable seed continuation stays bound to the authenticated export context.
Only verified portable seed artifacts install and synchronize.
